subject: Zinia
fact: Zinia is a master spy who decides that information must be obtained by talking to folks in a tavern looking for someone to buy them a drink.
source_quote: Zinia, always the master spy, decided that they needed information. The best way to get it was to talk to folks in a Tavern looking for someone to buy them a drink.

subject: tavern
fact: The tavern contains common folk, farmers, traders, and passers-by with no business or chores.
source_quote: Looking around, he noticed that these were all common folk, farmers, traders, and passers-by. It was midday, and these people had no business or chores.

subject: Black Jay
fact: The Black Jay is a mysterious and forlorn herdsman in league with local bandits who tips them off.
source_quote: One talked about a Black Jay. He was a mysterious and forlorn herdsman in league with local bandits. This mysterious man would tip the bandits off.

subject: Y’dey
fact: Y’dey, the head cleric of the village, has mysteriously disappeared, and the priest Terjon is closed-mouthed about the situation.
source_quote: The following person, a stout woman of indeterminate middle age, mutters that Y’dey, the head cleric of the village, has mysteriously disappeared. The priest, Terjon, is awfully closed-mouthed about the situation.

subject: Burne
fact: Burne is a youngish-looking man with a slight build, long brown hair, green eyes, and an aquiline nose, wearing a mage robe with scuff marks and scratches on it.
source_quote: Burne has a slight build, long brown hair, green eyes, and an aquiline nose. He’s wearing a mage robe with scuff marks and scratches on it.

subject: Rufus
fact: Rufus is a powerfully built man of average height with blue eyes, a delicate nose, and golden blond hair, wearing white linen pants and a dark blue blouse that shows more of his chest than anyone wants to see.
source_quote: Rufus is a powerfully built man of average height with blue eyes, a delicate nose, and golden blond hair. He is wearing white linen pants and a dark blue blouse that shows more of his chest than the Sequoia or anyone wants to see.

subject: castle tower
fact: The castle tower is 55 feet tall, with a smaller tower rising inside at about 35 feet above the ground, accessible only by a curving flight of stone stairs terminating in a landing 10 feet above the ground, with an outer door that lowers to form a bridge, arrow slits, a splay around the base to 6 feet in height, machicolated battlements, and pierced merlons.
source_quote: This structure is some 55 feet tall, a smaller tower rising inside the greater at about 35 feet above the ground. Its entrance is accessible only by going up a curving flight of stone stairs, which terminate in a landing about 10 feet above the ground. The outer door of the tower lowers to form a bridge to the stone landing. There are several arrow slits around the tower, and it has a splay around the base to about 6 feet in height. The lower and upper battlements are machicolated, and the merlons are pierced for archers.

subject: castle interior
fact: The castle interior has shuttered arrow slits flanking the door, two murder holes in the ceiling, two fireplaces where most cooking is done by two to three servants, a curved alcove for judgment, trestle tables extendable to accommodate 40 people, comfortable chairs along the walls, and walls hung with tapestries and decorated with 12 shields, four long swords, two broad swords, four spears, two battle axes, and the heads and homes of various creatures.
source_quote: Shuttered arrow slits flank the door to the room, and two murder holes are in the ceiling. Flanking the inner portal are two fireplaces, where most of the cooking is done by two to three servants. The lords of the place sit in judgment either here or at a table in the curved alcove. Trestle tables can be extended down and across to accommodate 40 people during a feast or revel. Several comfortable chairs are placed along the walls, and the walls themselves are hung with tapestries and decorated with shields, arms, and hunting trophies—12 shields, four long swords, two broad swords, four spears, two battle axes, and the heads and homes of various creatures.

subject: ramps in castle
fact: Ramps curving upwards and downwards lead to other levels in the castle.
source_quote: Ramps curving upwards and downwards lead to other levels.

subject: Jaroo
fact: Jaroo is the keeper of the blessed grove, a druid who looks at Zephyr with unmistakable disgust and thinks that Tieflings are outside the natural order and have no place in the prime material plane.
source_quote: Zephyr starts to ask him questions about what’s happening, but he notices that Jaroo looks at him with unmistakable disgust. Zephyr immediately realizes that Jaroo is a druid who thinks that Tieflings are outside the natural order and have no place in the prime material plane.

subject: grove
fact: The grove is a place of worship where the caretaker has neatly pruned the trees and the grass is well-tended, with a carefully placed line of bluish stones setting off the path to a rock cairn where flowers, nuts, berries, and leaf garlands are placed, and a small path leads beyond the shrine to a low-roofed wooden building placed under the great boughs of the central oaks of the thicket.
source_quote: The grove is a place of worship. The caretaker has neatly pruned the trees, and the grass is well-tended. A carefully placed line of bluish stones sets off the path to a rock cairn where flowers, nuts, berries, and leaf garlands are placed. A small path leads beyond the shrine to a low-roofed wooden building placed under the great boughs of the central oaks of the thicket.

subject: Jaroo
fact: Jaroo was sent to observe the events after the defeat of the Temple of Elemental Evil and is upset that Verbobonc isn’t interested in only protecting Hommlet but is also committed to absorbing the faithful into its Church.
source_quote: From the conversation, he learns that Jaroo was sent here to observe the events after the defeat of the Temple of Elemental Evil. Jaroo is upset that Verbobonc isn’t interested in only protecting Hommlet but is also committed to absorbing the faithful into its Church.

subject: Jaroo
fact: Jaroo distrusts the intentions of Burne and Rufus, and Terjon's goals.
source_quote: Jaroo distrusts the intentions of Burne and Rufus, and Terjon's goals.

subject: Moathouse
fact: The Moathouse was once the outpost of the Temple of Elemental Evil, its watchtower an advance base for raids, looting, and destruction, from which servants of the Temple were to bring the Village of Hommlet and all the lands around it into subjection, enslaving the conquered folk and forcing them to construct yet another fortress further west, spreading the evil power of the Temple in ever-growing rings to encompass all of the lands around its base.
source_quote: The mouthouse was once the outpost of the Temple of Elemental Evil, its watchtower an advance base for raids, looting, and destruction. From this area, servants of the Temple were to bring the Village of Hommlet and all the lands around it into subjection. The temple enslaved the conquered folk, and then they were forced to construct yet another fortress further west, spreading the evil power of the Temple in ever-growing rings to encompass all of the lands around its base.

subject: Emiry Meadows
fact: The Battle of Emiry Meadows ended the expansion of the Temple of Elemental Evil.
source_quote: This ended with the Battle of Emiry Meadows.

subject: Jaroo
fact: Jaroo tells the group that they must go and investigate the Moathouse and tell him and him alone, because the agents of the Temple may even be here, and Burne and Rufus may use whatever information they glean to restrict their freedoms.
source_quote: You must go and investigate the Moathouse. And when you have found what you are looking for, you must tell me and me alone. Do not tell anyone else because the agents of the Temple may even be here. As for Burne and Rufus, they may use whatever information they glean to restrict our freedoms.

subject: Rufus
fact: Rufus is the military commander of the area who deputizes the heroes, requiring them to share any information with him first, and threatening arrest or worse if they explore the Moathouse without his consent.
source_quote: I am the military commander of this area, and I am deputizing you. As my deputies, you are required to talk to me first. If you refuse my offer of being a deputy, I will have you arrested, or worse, if you explore the Moathouse. As my deputies, you are required to share any information with me, first. And then with anyone else.

subject: Burne
fact: Burne is horrified by the idea of the Temple of Elemental Evil's resurgence and agrees that such information must be presented to their boss in Verbobonc.
source_quote: Burne is horrified, “That’s impossible.” Rufus agrees and thinks momentarily, “My friends, if you were to find out that the temple was resurgent, that would be critical secret information. It would be essential that we present it to our boss in Verbobonc.”

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia smiles and nods to Rufus’s offer, having seen too many people with conflicting agendas, each trying to control the information flow, and decides that once he has information, he will decide what to share.
source_quote: Sequoia smiles and nods. He has seen too many people with too many conflicting agendas, each trying to control the information flow and accomplish something slightly different. Once he has information, he will decide what to share.

subject: Temple of St. Cuthbert
fact: The Temple of St. Cuthbert is a massive, imposing structure that is ridiculously too large for such a small village with so few souls.
source_quote: Zinia makes the long trek to the Temple of St. Cuthbert. A massive, imposing structure that is ridiculously too large for such a small village with so few souls.

subject: Terjon
fact: Terjon, the high priest, agrees that Calmer should join the group but requests that whatever information is obtained must be shared with him and him alone, because the safety of the good people of Oerth may hang in the balance.
source_quote: Terjon agrees with the idea that Calmer should join the group. But he does have one particular request that is so eerily familiar, “Whatever information you get must be shared with me and me alone. The safety of the good people of Oerth may hang in the balance.”

subject: Inn of the Welcome Wench
fact: The Inn of the Welcome Wench provides reasonable accommodations for reasonable prices, except for Zephyr, who is a spendthrift and demands the best room.
source_quote: From there, Zinia heads to the Inn of the Welcome Wench, where he and his traveling companions secure reasonable accommodations for reasonable prices, except for Zephyr, who is a spendthrift and demands the best room.

subject: Jaroo

source_quote: Jaroo pauses, “This ended with the Battle of Emiry Meadows.” He thinks some more and continues, “ The circles of outposts that you and your friends have uncovered are too early, similar to the plots of the original temple, to be a coincidence.”

source_quote: So, Zephyr leads the group to Jaroo, a local druid and follower of Beory. ... except for Zephyr, who is a spendthrift and demands the best room.
